scheme_name: Training for Horticulture Skill Development for Self-Employment at Centre of Excellence
description:
The Training for Horticulture Skill Development for Self-Employment at Centre of Excellence is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the skills of individuals in the horticulture sector.

This scheme was launched in 2014 as part of the National Horticulture Mission.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide skill development training to individuals in various aspects of horticulture.

The goal is to empower at least 1 lakh individuals annually through skill development in horticulture.

The training encompasses various areas such as nursery management, organic farming, post-harvest management, and value addition.

Participants are trained to develop competencies that will enable them to start their own horticulture-related enterprises.

The scheme aims to increase employment opportunities in the horticulture sector.

It also seeks to promote self-employment among youth and women in rural areas.

The benefits of this scheme include hands-on training and exposure to modern horticulture practices.

Participants receive training from experts in the field of horticulture.

The training is conducted at various Centres of Excellence across the country.

Each Centre of Excellence is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities and resources.

The training duration typically ranges from 15 days to 6 months depending on the specific course.

Participants are provided with training materials and resources at no cost.

The scheme also includes practical training sessions in the field.

Upon successful completion of the training, participants receive a certificate.

This certificate enhances their employability in the horticulture sector.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include individuals aged between 18 to 45 years.

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for the training.

However, individuals with a background in agriculture or horticulture may have an advantage.

The income criteria for eligibility is not strictly defined.

The application process involves several steps.

Interested candidates must visit the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

They can find information about the nearest Centre of Excellence.

Candidates are required to fill out an application form available at the Centre.

They must submit the completed form along with a copy of their identification proof.

Documents required include an Aadhaar card or any government-issued ID.

Candidates may also need to provide a passport-sized photograph.

After submitting the application, candidates will be notified about the training schedule.

The training sessions are conducted periodically throughout the year.

The frequency of training sessions varies by Centre of Excellence.

Disbursement of training certificates occurs immediately upon completion of the course.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The specific department responsible for the execution of this scheme is the Department of Horticulture.

Each Centre of Excellence is managed by state agricultural universities or research institutions.

Contact details for inquiries can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture.

The scheme also collaborates with various agricultural universities to enhance training quality.

Statistical data indicates that over 50,000 individuals have benefited from this scheme since its inception.

The training has led to the establishment of numerous self-employment ventures in horticulture.

Participants have reported increased income levels post-training.

The scheme also contributes to the overall growth of the horticulture sector in India.

The horticulture sector has seen a growth rate of approximately 4.5% annually.

This growth is attributed to the increased adoption of modern techniques and practices.

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

It also supports the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative by promoting self-reliance.

The training covers sustainable practices that are environmentally friendly.

Participants learn about integrated pest management and organic farming techniques.

The scheme encourages the use of technology in horticulture.

Digital tools and applications are introduced to participants for better farm management.

The training also emphasizes the importance of market linkages for horticulture products.

Participants are taught how to access markets and sell their produce effectively.

The scheme has received positive feedback from participants and stakeholders alike.

Success stories of individuals who have started their own businesses are highlighted.

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the impact of the scheme.

Future plans include expanding the number of Centres of Excellence across the country.

The scheme aims to reach more remote areas to benefit underprivileged communities.

Training modules are regularly updated to include the latest advancements in horticulture.

The government also seeks to collaborate with private sector players to enhance training outcomes.

This initiative is part of a broader strategy to boost the agricultural economy in India.

The horticulture sector is crucial for food security and nutritional needs.

The scheme plays a vital role in promoting entrepreneurship among the youth.

It also addresses unemployment issues in rural areas by providing skill development.

Overall, the Training for Horticulture Skill Development for Self-Employment at Centre of Excellence is a comprehensive initiative.

It aims to create a skilled workforce in the horticulture sector.

The scheme not only benefits individuals but also contributes to the agricultural economy of India.
